Marine Biology, MS
Earn Your Master's Degree in Marine Biology
On Campus
32
Credit Hours
2 Years
Avg Completion
At Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi, marine biology students learn from internationally recognized faculty and gain hands-on research experience in one of North America's most distinctive coastal environments. Through advanced coursework, field experiences, and original research, students develop the knowledge, technical skills, and scientific expertise needed to make meaningful contributions to marine science and build successful careers in the field.
Program Details
The Master of Science in Marine Biology is a research-focused graduate program for students who want to deepen their understanding of marine organisms—including their physiology and evolution, as well as the ecosystems they inhabit—explore applied fields such as conservation, fisheries and biotechnology, and help advance marine biological research. Through advanced coursework, laboratory experiences, field studies and independent research, students examine the complex challenges facing marine organisms and ecosystems while developing the skills needed for careers in research, conservation, government, education and industry.
Most students complete the program in approximately two years while working closely with faculty mentors on original research projects. Students have access to specialized laboratories, biological analytical facilities, marine population and ecosystem observation technologies, and research vessels that support wetland, coastal, and offshore studies. Located on its own island campus along the Texas coast, Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi provides direct access to diverse and unique marine and coastal ecosystems, creating exceptional opportunities for scientific discovery and hands-on learning.
Researchers in Action
TAMU-CC's Marine Biology faculty and student researchers investigate topics spanning botany and phycology, microbiology, molecular, cellular, organismal and population biology, fisheries biology, aquaculture and mariculture, microbial interactions and microbiomes, anatomy, physiology, behavior, genetics, evolution, and marine and wetland ecology.
What You'll Learn
The Marine Biology, MS combines advanced coursework with faculty-mentored research to prepare students for professional and scientific careers in marine biology. Coursework and research experiences emphasize:
Marine biology comprises multiple biological disciplines: ecology, zoology, botany/phycology, microbiology, physiology, genetics and molecular biology, evolution and systematics, behavior and interaction
Experimental design and hypothesis-driven research
Statistical and computational analysis
Marine field techniques and laboratory methods
Data collection, management, and interpretation
Scientific writing and communication
Research ethics, data transparency, and reproducibility
Interdisciplinary collaboration and problem-solving
Professional presentation of scientific findings
Throughout the program, students design and conduct original research while developing the analytical, technical and communication skills needed to advance the study of marine biology, evolution and adaptation of marine organisms, marine ecology, marine habitats, and interdisciplinary areas such as fisheries biology, aquaculture and mariculture, conservation, biotechnology, physiology, toxicology, pathology and disease ecology.

Career Outcomes
The Marine Biology, MS prepares graduates for careers in marine biology, conservation, education, government, and industry. Through advanced scientific training and hands-on research, students develop the knowledge and technical skills needed to address the complex environmental, ecological and biological challenges affecting marine organisms, advance scientific discovery, and contribute to the stewardship of marine organisms, populations and ecosystems.
Graduates pursue careers such as:
Marine Biologist
Research Scientist
Environmental Consultant
Fisheries Scientist
Coastal Resource Manager
Conservation Scientist
Marine Policy Analyst
Science Educator
Laboratory Manager
Scientific Program Coordinator
Marine biology professionals work in universities, research institutions, federal and state agencies, nonprofit organizations, aquariums, and private industry. Whether your goal is to conduct research, inform environmental policy, protect natural resources, or educate future generations, the Marine Biology, MS provides the foundation you need to make an impact.
Salary & Job Outlook
Marine biology graduates pursue a wide range of career paths, making salary potential highly dependent on role, employer, location, and experience. As demand grows for professionals who can conduct research, analyze biological data, and address complex biological challenges, graduate-level training can provide a competitive advantage in the field. The Marine Biology, MS prepares students with the advanced knowledge, research experience, and technical expertise sought by employers across the public, private, and nonprofit sectors.
The TAMU-CC Advantage
Marine biology students at TAMU-CC benefit from a powerful combination of expert faculty, advanced research facilities, access to diverse research topics, and a location that provides unparalleled access to unique marine ecosystems.
Learn from Researchers Shaping the Future of Marine Science
Marine Biology students work alongside internationally recognized faculty whose research spans topics ranging from molecular biology and genetics to ecosystem science. Faculty direct active research programs, publish in leading scientific journals, and secure competitive grants that support innovative research and student involvement. Rather than simply learning about marine biology in the classroom, students have opportunities to contribute to the discovery process alongside scientists advancing the field.
Study in One of North America's Most Distinctive Coastal Environments
Location matters in marine biology.
Situated on its own island campus along the Texas coast, Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi provides direct access to globally unique marine ecosystems, including bays, estuaries, barrier islands, wetlands, seagrass meadows, tidal flats, and offshore waters. The region is also home to the Laguna Madre, one of the world's few hypersaline lagoon systems and one of the most significant coastal environments in North America for marine biology research.
This remarkable diversity allows students to study marine organisms and ecological processes across multiple habitats without traveling far from campus. Access to coastal wetlands, seagrass meadows, and offshore ecosystems, allows students to gain hands-on experience in marine ecology, molecular biology, anatomy, physiology, behavior in marine environments that support globally important fisheries, migratory bird populations, and coastal wildlife.
Gain Experience Through Active Research
Research is not reserved for faculty members.
From the beginning of the program, students work closely with faculty mentors to develop research questions, design studies, analyze data, and communicate scientific findings. Opportunities may include field-based investigations, laboratory research, interdisciplinary collaborations, conference presentations, publications, and participation in funded research projects.
These experiences help students build the confidence, technical expertise, and professional credentials needed for careers in research, education, government, and industry.
Access Advanced Facilities and Technology
Students have access to the tools used by today's marine scientists. Specialized laboratories, marine analytical facilities, molecular research technologies, ocean observing systems, and research vessels support investigations ranging from genetics and physiology to organism biology, fisheries science, and ecosystem ecology.
These resources allow students to develop practical experience with modern scientific techniques while preparing for advanced research, professional positions, and leadership opportunities in marine biology.
Join a Community Dedicated to Discovery
Marine biology at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is built on collaboration. Students work closely with faculty mentors, fellow researchers, and scientific partners while becoming part of a community committed to the advancement of marine biology.
Whether your goal is to pursue a Ph.D., conduct research or build a career in ecosystem management, aquaculture or marine conservation, you’ll graduate prepared to confidently take the next step.
Want to learn more? Fill out our contact form and a graduate admissions counselor will connect with you soon.
How to Apply
Applying is much easier when you're supported—and at TAMU-CC, our graduate admissions counselors are here to help.
To get started, you’ll need a bachelor's degree in any subject from an accredited institution.
To apply, you will need to submit:
Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
A current resume or curriculum vitae (CV)
A statement of purpose (maximum 1,000 words) describing your educational and career goals, research interests, and how they align with the Marine Biology faculty. Applicants should also include the names of faculty members they have contacted regarding potential research opportunities.
Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to your academic, research, or professional qualifications.
GRE scores are not required for admission.
International Students also submit:
English proficiency scores and Visa documentation

Frequently Asked Questions
Is the Marine Biology M.S. offered online?
No. The program is offered in person to provide students with hands-on research and field experiences.
Do I need a degree in marine biology to apply?
No. Students from related academic backgrounds may be considered. Admission depends on preparation, research interests, and faculty advisor approval. Additional prerequisite coursework may be required.
Is a thesis required?
Yes. Students complete a faculty-mentored thesis based on original research conducted during the program. The thesis process includes developing a research proposal, conducting independent research, preparing a written thesis, and successfully defending the research before a graduate committee.
Are assistantships available?
Teaching assistantships may be available, particularly when research funding is not available through a faculty mentor.
How long does the program take to complete?
Most students complete the degree in approximately two years.
How do I find a faculty advisor?
Applicants are encouraged to review faculty research interests and contact potential advisors before applying. Admission requires a faculty member who agrees to mentor the student's graduate research.
